summary: Emil Kowalski's animate-expo skill is a build sequence for motion in React Native and Expo apps: decide whether something should animate at all, name its purpose, pick the cheapest tool, pick cheap properties, choose spring or timing from fixed tables, keep the work on the UI thread, redesign hover as press, add haptics carefully, and ship reduced motion with the animation. It starts from three facts about mobile: there is no hover, there are two runtimes (React Native and the UI thread), and the user's finger is on the element. It gives exact spring configs, three bezier curves, duration bands, haptic calls per moment, touch-target sizes and a Never Ship table. For a design system this is a ready set of mobile motion tokens and guardrails, plus a rule that feel is only verified on a release build on the slowest supported device.
key_ideas: Mobile motion rests on three facts: no hover, two runtimes, and a finger on the element.
The worst failure is animating something that should not animate; the frequency gate can mean writing no code.
How often a person sees an animation decides whether it animates: 100+ times a day means none.
Every animation needs a one-word purpose; without one, it is not built.
Use the cheapest tool that works, and prefer the platform's native navigation, sheets, tabs and menus over JS rebuilds.
Only transform and opacity are free; layout properties re-run layout for the node and its siblings every frame.
If a finger was involved, use a spring and hand it the gesture's velocity; otherwise use timing with a strong ease-out.
Springs are set with duration and damping ratio (Apple's designer parameters), not mass, stiffness and damping.
Keep motion off the JS thread: no setState per frame, no per-frame calls back to React Native, no shared-value reads in render.
Hover has to be redesigned as press: feedback on press-in, commit on press-out, a 0.97 scale in 100-150ms.
Haptics fire in the same frame as the visual, once per user action, and never as the only feedback.
Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not zero: keep opacity and color, drop movement, scale, parallax and overshoot.
Feel is only verified on a release build on the slowest supported device, never in Expo Go or the simulator.
Navigation motion matches the platform; everything else beats it and stays under 300ms.

entities.name: Lottie

entities.name: React Native Skia

entities.name: Yoga
entities.description: React Native's layout engine; animating layout properties re-runs it every frame for the node and its siblings.

entities.name: React Compiler

entities.name: Expo Go

entities.name: ProMotion

entities.name: Frequency gate

entities.name: Velocity handoff

topics.name: Motion principles
topics.summary: A gated build order: frequency tier, one-word purpose, cheapest tool, cheap properties, spring vs timing, thread, press, haptics, reduced motion.

topics.name: Easing and timing
topics.summary: ease-out for enter/exit and default, ease-in-out for on-screen movement, linear for constant motion, never ease-in; three custom beziers; duration bands of 100-150ms, 150-200ms and ~300ms, all under 300ms except platform navigation.

topics.name: Spring animation
topics.summary: Springs whenever a finger was involved, configured with duration and dampingRatio from a fixed table, velocity passed in, overshootClamping at hard edges, bounce only after momentum.

topics.name: Animation performance
topics.summary: Only transform and opacity are free; keep motion on the UI runtime; no setState or scheduleOnRN per frame; no animated elevation or BlurView intensity; enable 120fps on ProMotion; verify on a release build on the slowest device.

topics.name: Gestures and drag
topics.summary: Gesture.Pan() instead of PanResponder, interruptibility and velocity handoff as baseline, velocity-or-distance dismissal and rubber-band resistance at boundaries.

topics.name: Micro-interactions
topics.summary: Press feedback on press-in with scale 0.97 in 100-150ms, and haptics mapped to selection, snap, heavy landing and success or error.

topics.name: Reduced motion
topics.summary: Ship it with the animation; keep opacity and color changes, drop translation, scale, parallax and overshoot; screen transitions become fade.

topics.name: Mobile app patterns
topics.summary: No hover on mobile; use native stack transitions, formSheet, NativeTabs, native menus, large-title headers, RefreshControl and keyboard-controller instead of JS rebuilds.

topics.name: Drawers and sheets
topics.summary: A sheet that is its own screen uses presentation: 'formSheet'; sheet and drawer springs use duration 300 and dampingRatio 0.8 with velocity.

topics.name: Navigation and sidebars
topics.summary: Tab switches never slide (animation: 'none'); screen transitions use the platform default and are never overridden or hand-rolled.

topics.name: Buttons and actions
topics.summary: Pressables scale to 0.97 on press-in, commit on press-out, keep a 44x44pt / 48dp target via hitSlop, and use pressRetentionOffset.

topics.name: Accessibility
topics.summary: Reduced motion support, minimum touch targets, haptics never the only feedback, and no hardcoded heights, because a height measured at default type size is wrong at 200% text size.

rules.rule: On mobile, move every hover affordance into press, position, or nothing; redesign it rather than porting it from the web.
rules.why: There is no hover on mobile.
rules.evidence: There is no hover.; 7. Press, not hover

rules.rule: Keep every React Native animation on the UI runtime (worklets), never on the React Native runtime.
rules.why: An animation that touches the RN runtime stutters the moment the app does anything else.

rules.rule: Treat interruptibility and velocity handoff as the baseline for anything a finger touches, not as polish.
rules.why: Gestures are the primary input on mobile; the user's finger is on the element.
rules.evidence: The user's finger is on the element.

rules.rule: When building motion, make the call, state the reasoning in one line and write the code; do not present motion options as a menu.
rules.why: The skill's posture is a senior mobile engineer building the animation.

rules.rule: Do not animate something that should not animate; the gate may correctly produce zero lines of code.
rules.why: Animating something that shouldn't animate is the worse of the two failure modes.
rules.evidence: Operating Posture: Two failure modes, and the first is worse

rules.rule: Never drive an animation with a setState per frame, a PanResponder or an animated height.
rules.why: It looks fine in dev on your phone and drops to 20fps on a three-year-old Android.
rules.evidence: Animating the right thing on the wrong thread

rules.rule: Run the build sequence in order; steps 1 (should it animate) and 2 (what is the purpose) gate everything else.
rules.why: The gate exists to stop motion that should not be built.

rules.rule: Use Reanimated, not React Native's core Animated.
rules.why: Core Animated can't be driven by a gesture without crossing the bridge, and useNativeDriver refuses anything but transform and opacity; Reanimated worklets run on the UI thread and keep running while JS is busy.
rules.evidence: Reanimated worklets run on the UI thread and keep running while JS is busy

rules.rule: Take curves and spring configs from the skill's tables; never approximate values.
rules.why: Hard rule: no approximated values.

rules.rule: Ship reduced-motion support with the animation, not as a follow-up.
rules.why: Hard rule 4.

rules.rule: Judge animation feel only on a release build on the slowest device you support.
rules.why: Nothing else counts as verified.

rules.rule: Do not animate interactions seen 100+ times a day (tab switches, keyboard open/close, scrolling, settings toggles); use the platform default or nothing.
rules.why: Frequency gate: at 100+ times a day the decision is platform default or nothing; stop here.

rules.rule: For interactions seen tens of times a day (press feedback, list navigation, row selection), use only near-imperceptible motion under 150ms, or nothing.
rules.why: Frequency gate.

rules.rule: Give occasional elements (sheets, modals, toasts, onboarding steps) standard animation.
rules.why: Frequency gate: occasional tier.

rules.rule: Spend the delight budget only on rare or first-time moments (success states, empty-state illustrations, celebration).
rules.why: The delight budget lives in the rare tier.

rules.rule: Never slide between tabs; set animation: 'none'.
rules.why: Tabs are peers, not a hierarchy; sliding implies depth that isn't there, and the user pays for it dozens of times a session.

rules.rule: If a requested animation fails the frequency gate, say so and don't write it.
rules.why: Gate result.
rules.evidence: If the request fails this gate, say so and don't write it.

rules.rule: Name the purpose of each animation in one word before building it: feedback, spatial consistency, state indication, preventing a jarring change, explanation, or delight (rare tier only); if you can't name it, don't build it.
rules.why: An animation with no nameable purpose should not exist.

rules.rule: Pick the cheapest tool that works by walking down the tool table and stopping at the first that fits.
rules.why: Cheapest that works.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool — cheapest that works

rules.rule: Use a Reanimated CSS transition (transitionProperty in the style) for a state-driven change with no gesture: press, toggle, color, a value flipping.
rules.why: Cheapest tool for state changes.

rules.rule: Use a Reanimated CSS animation (animationName keyframes) for loops, multi-stage motion, or motion that plays on mount with no state change.
rules.why: Tool table.

rules.rule: Use layout animations (entering / exiting / itemLayoutAnimation) for elements mounting or unmounting and for list reflow.
rules.why: Tool table.

rules.rule: Use useSharedValue + Gesture + useAnimatedStyle for anything a finger touches or anything derived from scroll.
rules.why: Tool table.

rules.rule: Use native stack options in Expo Router for screen-to-screen transitions; never hand-roll them.
rules.why: Tool table: never hand-roll this.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: Screen to screen

rules.rule: Use presentation: 'formSheet' for a bottom sheet that is its own screen.
rules.why: It's a real UISheetPresentationController, free and correct.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: A bottom sheet that is its own screen

rules.rule: Use NativeTabs (from expo-router/unstable-native-tabs) for the tab bar.
rules.why: It is the platform's real tab bar, with its behaviors and transitions included.
rules.evidence: the platform's real tab bar, its behaviors and transitions included

rules.rule: Use Link.Menu / Link.Preview (Expo Router) for context menus and press-and-hold previews; never rebuild them in JS.
rules.why: They are native menus and peek (iOS-only).
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: Context menu, press-and-hold preview

rules.rule: For a header that collapses into a large title, use headerLargeTitleEnabled on the native stack, not a scroll worklet.
rules.why: Native behavior (iOS-only); headerLargeTitle is deprecated.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: Header that collapses into a large title

rules.rule: Use RefreshControl for pull to refresh; hand-roll it only when it is a signature interaction.
rules.why: Tool table.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: Pull to refresh

rules.rule: Use react-native-keyboard-controller for UI that tracks the keyboard.
rules.why: It gives the keyboard's real position, frame by frame, on the UI thread.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: UI that tracks the keyboard

rules.rule: Use Lottie only for vector illustration, celebration and empty states; never for UI state.
rules.why: Tool table: illustration only.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: Vector illustration, celebration, empty state

rules.rule: Use @shopify/react-native-skia for a huge animated scene or freeform drawing, when the view hierarchy itself is the bottleneck.
rules.why: A canvas avoids the view hierarchy.
rules.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: A huge animated scene, freeform drawing

rules.rule: Reach for a shared value only when the value is continuous or interruptible: a press scale is a CSS transition, a drag is a shared value.
rules.why: Using a worklet for a two-state toggle is the mobile equivalent of installing a motion library for a fade.
rules.evidence: Reach for a shared value only when

rules.rule: Install motion packages with npx expo install <package>, not plain npm install.
rules.why: It resolves the version that matches the project's SDK, which plain npm install won't.

rules.rule: Use react-native-reanimated + react-native-worklets for animation, react-native-gesture-handler for gestures, expo-router for navigation, sheets, native tabs and menus, expo-haptics for haptics, react-native-keyboard-controller (with KeyboardProvider at the root) for keyboard-following UI, lottie-react-native for illustration, and @shopify/react-native-skia for very large scenes.
rules.why: Dependency table.

rules.rule: Animate only transform and opacity; do not animate width, height, margin, padding, flex, top, left or gap (the one exception is an absolutely positioned element with no children).
rules.why: transform and opacity are free; the others re-run Yoga on every frame for that node and its siblings.

rules.rule: When an absolutely positioned element with no children (a tab pill, a progress bar fill) has to change size, animate its width rather than scaleX; it is the only exception to transform and opacity.
rules.why: It's out of flow, so nothing else re-lays-out, and width keeps the corner radius that scaleX would smear.
rules.evidence: The one exception: an absolutely positioned element with no children

rules.rule: Never enter from scale(0); start from scale(0.9–0.97) plus opacity: 0.
rules.why: Nothing in the real world appears from nothing.

rules.rule: Put translate before scale in a React Native transform array unless you want the translate multiplied.
rules.why: transform is an array and order matters: [{ translateY }, { scale }] scales after moving; reversed, the translate gets scaled too.
rules.evidence: transform is an array and order matters

rules.rule: On Android, never animate elevation; animate the opacity of a pre-shadowed layer instead.
rules.why: Android shadows are elevation, and animating elevation re-renders the shadow every frame.

rules.rule: Never animate BlurView intensity; crossfade the opacity of a static BlurView instead.
rules.why: On Android it re-renders the blur each frame.

rules.rule: Use percentage translates to move an element by its own size, e.g. translateY('100%') to move a sheet by its own height.
rules.why: Percentages in translate are relative to the element's own size, whatever its content.

rules.rule: If a finger was involved, use a spring; use timing for everything else.
rules.why: Springs carry velocity through an interruption; timing curves restart.

rules.rule: Configure Reanimated springs with duration and dampingRatio (Apple's two designer parameters), not mass/stiffness/damping.
rules.why: Reanimated's spring takes Apple's two designer parameters directly.

rules.rule: Use { duration: 400, dampingRatio: 1 } for a default settle with no overshoot.
rules.why: Spring table.
rules.evidence: 5. Timing or spring: Default settle, no overshoot

rules.rule: Use { duration: 400, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity } to reposition or snap back after a drag.
rules.why: Spring table.
rules.evidence: 5. Timing or spring: Reposition / snap back after a drag

rules.rule: Use { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity } for sheets and drawers.
rules.why: Spring table.

rules.rule: Add overshootClamping: true to any spring that must not pass a hard edge.
rules.why: Spring table.
rules.evidence: 5. Timing or spring: Must not pass a hard edge

rules.rule: Allow bounce (overshoot) only when the gesture carried momentum.
rules.why: Overshoot on a menu that faded in feels wrong; overshoot on a card you flicked feels right.
rules.evidence: Bounce only when the gesture carried momentum.

rules.rule: Use ease-out for elements entering or exiting, and as the default easing.
rules.why: Easing table for motion without a finger on it.
rules.evidence: Easing, for everything without a finger on it

rules.rule: Use ease-in-out for elements moving or morphing on screen.
rules.why: Easing table.

rules.rule: Use linear easing for constant motion such as progress and marquees.
rules.why: Easing table.

rules.rule: Never use ease-in (Easing.in(...)) on a UI element.
rules.why: It starts slow, delaying the exact moment the user is watching.
rules.evidence: It starts slow, delaying the exact moment the user is watching

rules.rule: Do not use Reanimated's built-in easings; use custom bezier curves instead.
rules.why: Reanimated's built-ins are as weak as CSS's.
rules.evidence: Reanimated's built-ins are as weak as CSS's

rules.rule: Use Easing.bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) as the strong ease-out for UI.
rules.why: Named EASE_OUT: strong ease-out for UI.

rules.rule: Use Easing.bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1) for on-screen movement.
rules.why: Named EASE_IN_OUT: on-screen movement.

rules.rule: Use Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) as the iOS sheet curve.
rules.why: Named EASE_SHEET: iOS sheet curve.

rules.rule: Give press feedback a duration of 100–150ms.
rules.why: Duration table.

rules.rule: Give toggles, chips and small state changes a duration of 150–200ms.
rules.why: Duration table.
rules.evidence: Duration: Toggle, chip, small state change

rules.rule: Animate sheets, modals and drawers with a spring of about 300ms perceived duration.
rules.why: Duration table.

rules.rule: Use the platform default duration for screen transitions; don't override it.
rules.why: Match the platform for navigation.

rules.rule: Keep mobile UI animations under 300ms, the same as web; match the platform only for navigation (iOS push is 350ms) and beat it everywhere else.
rules.why: The platform's own transitions are longer; UI motion should be quicker.
rules.evidence: Mobile UI animations stay under 300ms, same as web.

rules.rule: Never call setState from a gesture or scroll handler; drive the style from a shared value through useAnimatedStyle.
rules.why: One React render per frame is the single biggest cause of jank in RN apps; with a shared value React never re-renders.
rules.evidence: 6. Keep it off the JS thread

rules.rule: Never call scheduleOnRN inside onUpdate or a scroll handler; call it in onEnd, or in a useAnimatedReaction that fires when a value crosses a threshold.
rules.why: In onUpdate it queues an RN-runtime call 60–120× per second.
rules.evidence: Never schedule back to the RN runtime inside onUpdate

rules.rule: Use scheduleOnRN(fn, ...args) from react-native-worklets instead of the deprecated runOnJS(fn)(...args).
rules.why: runOnJS is deprecated in Reanimated 4.
rules.evidence: 6. Keep it off the JS thread; Never Ship

rules.rule: Never read a shared value during render (for example translateY.get() in JSX).
rules.why: It's a snapshot that never updates and it silently desyncs.
rules.evidence: Never read a shared value during render

rules.rule: Never write a shared value during render; touch shared values only in worklets, handlers and effects.
rules.why: It fires mid-reconciliation, and a re-render you didn't cause replays the write.
rules.evidence: Never write one during render either

rules.rule: Access shared values with .get() / .set(), not .value; use the functional form sv.set((v) => v + 1) for updates based on the current value.
rules.why: Direct .value access is the form the React Compiler can't see through; get/set is the compiler-safe way.

rules.rule: Put 'worklet' as the first line of any function called from a worklet.
rules.why: Otherwise they throw at runtime on device while working fine in the debugger.
rules.evidence: Functions called from a worklet need 'worklet'

rules.rule: Show feedback on press-in and commit the action on press-out.
rules.why: Waiting for the tap to complete before showing anything feels dead; this is the latency the user perceives.
rules.evidence: Feedback on press-in, commit on press-out.

rules.rule: Scale every pressable to 0.97 in 100–150ms, using Pressable plus a CSS transition.
rules.why: Scale takes the label and icons with it, which is what makes it read as physical.
rules.evidence: on any pressable, `Pressable` + a CSS transition

rules.rule: Make touch targets at least 44×44pt on iOS.
rules.why: Minimum touch target.

rules.rule: Make touch targets at least 48dp on Android.
rules.why: Minimum touch target.

rules.rule: When the visual is smaller than the minimum target, add hitSlop instead of growing the visual.
rules.why: Stated with the 44×44pt minimum: meet the target without growing the visual.
rules.evidence: If the visual is smaller, add hitSlop

rules.rule: Set pressRetentionOffset on pressables.
rules.why: A finger drifting a few pixels shouldn't cancel a press the user meant.

rules.rule: Use the Android ripple only in a Material-styled app; in a custom-designed app use the same press scale on both platforms.
rules.why: The same scale on both platforms is more coherent than a ripple on one.
rules.evidence: Android ripple only in a Material-styled app.

rules.rule: Fire Haptics.selectionAsync() when a value ticks past a step: picker, slider detent, segmented control.
rules.why: Haptic mapping table.

rules.rule: Fire Haptics.impactAsync(ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light) when something snaps home, a sheet detent catches, or a drag commits.
rules.why: Haptic mapping table.

rules.rule: Fire Haptics.impactAsync(ImpactFeedbackStyle.Medium) when a heavy object lands or a destructive action fires.
rules.why: Haptic mapping table.

rules.rule: Fire Haptics.notificationAsync(NotificationFeedbackType.Success / Error) when an operation succeeds or fails.
rules.why: Haptic mapping table.

rules.rule: Fire a haptic in the same frame as its visual, at the causal moment (the detent catching), not when the animation finishes.
rules.why: A haptic that lags its animation reads as a glitch, not as feedback.

rules.rule: Use at most one haptic per user action: never on scroll, never per frame, never on an entrance animation the user didn't cause.
rules.why: Used sparingly haptics make the app feel expensive; used everywhere, users turn them off.

rules.rule: Never make a haptic the only feedback; always pair it with a visual that stands alone.
rules.why: Haptics are off system-wide for many users, and silent on most Android hardware.

rules.rule: From a worklet, schedule haptics back to the React Native runtime, e.g. scheduleOnRN(Haptics.selectionAsync).
rules.why: Haptics must run on the RN runtime.
rules.evidence: From a worklet, haptics must be scheduled back

rules.rule: Read reduced motion with useReducedMotion(), or pass reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System to each animation.
rules.why: Reduced motion ships with the animation; the snippet shows both forms.

rules.rule: Under reduced motion, keep opacity and color changes that explain a state change and drop translation, scale, parallax and overshoot.
rules.why: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not zero.
rules.evidence: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not zero

rules.rule: Under reduced motion, switch screen transitions to animation: 'fade'.
rules.why: Reduced-motion screen transition.

rules.rule: Never animate to a hardcoded height; measure with onLayout, or animate a transform instead.
rules.why: allowFontScaling is on by default, so any height measured at default type size is wrong at 200%.

rules.rule: Install Reanimated through Expo (npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets) and rely on babel-preset-expo for the worklets Babel plugin; in a bare React Native project without that preset, add the plugin manually and last in the list.
rules.why: A missing or misplaced plugin throws 'Failed to create a worklet' at runtime.

rules.rule: When using react-native-keyboard-controller for keyboard-following UI, put KeyboardProvider at the root.
rules.why: The dependency table says it needs KeyboardProvider at the root.

rules.rule: Wrap the app in GestureHandlerRootView.
rules.why: Without it, gestures do nothing with no error.

rules.rule: Run the app on the New Architecture when using Reanimated 4.
rules.why: Reanimated 4 requires the New Architecture.

rules.rule: Never judge animation feel in Expo Go, a dev build or the simulator; use a release build on the slowest supported device.
rules.why: A dev build's JS thread is slow enough to hide exactly the problems you're looking for.
rules.evidence: Expo Go is not a performance environment.; Never Ship table

rules.rule: Confirm CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone is true in expo.ios.infoPlist, and add it if missing.
rules.why: On ProMotion iPhones, third-party animations are capped at 60fps unless it is set; with it the frame budget is 8ms, not 16.

rules.rule: When a request matches a recipe (press feedback, drag-to-dismiss sheet, swipe-to-delete, collapsing header, list entrances, keyboard-synced UI, tab indicator, screen transitions), start from the recipe rather than a blank file.
rules.why: Recipes are ready-to-build implementations.

rules.rule: Never use PanResponder; use Gesture.Pan() from gesture-handler.
rules.why: Never Ship table.

rules.rule: Never use core Animated for anything a finger touches; use Reanimated.
rules.why: Never Ship table.

rules.rule: Never put entering on a virtualized list row; animate the container, or use itemLayoutAnimation.
rules.why: Never Ship table.

rules.rule: Never rebuild a screen transition in JS; use the native stack animation option.
rules.why: Never Ship table.

rules.rule: Never use a distance-only dismissal threshold; dismiss on velocity or distance, so a flick is enough.
rules.why: Never Ship table.

rules.rule: Never hard-stop an element at a boundary; apply rubber-band resistance.
rules.why: Never Ship table.
rules.evidence: Never Ship: Hard stop at a boundary

rules.rule: After writing motion code, report in a few lines: the gate result (frequency tier, named purpose, and what was rejected and why), the ingredients (tool, properties, spring or curve plus duration, thread), and what to feel-check on device (flick it, interrupt it mid-flight, reverse it, run it on the slowest Android).
rules.why: Gestures, velocity handoff and haptic timing cannot be judged from code.

rules.rule: Do not pad the motion deliverable into a report; the code is the deliverable.
rules.why: Output section.
rules.evidence: The code is the deliverable. Don't pad it into a report.

rules.rule: Say it plainly when the honest answer is that something shouldn't animate, or that it needs a real device before its feel can be judged.
rules.why: Tone: opinionated and brief.

decisions.question: Should this element animate at all, given how often people see it?

options.name: No animation (100+ times/day)
options.effect: Platform default or nothing; tab switches, keyboard open/close, scrolling and settings toggles stay instant.

options.name: Near-imperceptible (tens of times/day)
options.effect: Under 150ms or nothing; press feedback, list navigation, row selection.
options.when: Interactions seen tens of times a day.

options.name: Standard animation (occasional)
options.effect: Normal enter/exit motion for sheets, modals, toasts, onboarding steps.

options.name: Delight (rare / first-time)
options.effect: Where the delight budget is spent: success states, empty-state illustrations, celebration.

decisions.recommendation: Decide by frequency; anything seen 100+ times a day gets no animation, and a request that fails the gate is not built.

decisions.question: Which tool should build the motion in a React Native app?

options.name: Reanimated CSS transition
options.effect: Declarative transitionProperty in the style; no shared value or worklet.
options.when: State-driven change with no gesture: press, toggle, color.

options.name: Reanimated CSS animation
options.when: Loops, multi-stage, or plays on mount with no state change.

options.name: Shared value + Gesture + useAnimatedStyle
options.when: Anything a finger touches or anything derived from scroll.

options.name: Native platform components
options.effect: Native stack options, formSheet, NativeTabs, Link.Menu / Link.Preview, headerLargeTitleEnabled, RefreshControl.
options.when: Screen transitions, sheets that are screens, tab bars, context menus, large-title headers, pull to refresh.

options.name: Lottie or Skia
options.when: Illustration and celebration (Lottie); huge scenes or freeform drawing (Skia).

decisions.recommendation: Walk down the table and stop at the first tool that fits; prefer the cheapest, and never hand-roll what the platform provides.
decisions.evidence: 3. Pick the tool — cheapest that works

decisions.question: Should a piece of motion use a spring or a timing curve?

options.name: Spring
options.effect: Carries velocity through an interruption, so grabbing or reversing mid-flight stays fluid.

options.name: Timing (easing + duration)
options.when: Everything without a finger on it.

decisions.recommendation: Spring if a finger was involved; timing for everything else.

decisions.question: How should springs be configured?

options.name: Duration + dampingRatio (Apple's designer parameters)
options.effect: Default settle {400, 1}; drag snap-back {400, 0.8, velocity}; sheet or drawer {300, 0.8, velocity}; overshootClamping at hard edges.

options.name: Mass / stiffness / damping
options.when: The source says not to use this form.

decisions.recommendation: Use duration and dampingRatio from the table, and bounce only when the gesture carried momentum.

decisions.question: Which easing curve fits each situation?

options.name: ease-in
options.effect: Starts slow, delaying the moment the user watches.

decisions.recommendation: ease-out by default with the custom bezier; never ease-in; never Reanimated's built-in curves.
decisions.evidence: Easing, for everything without a finger on it

decisions.question: How long should each kind of mobile animation be?
decisions.recommendation: Stay under 300ms for UI; match the platform only for navigation.

decisions.question: Should screen transitions follow the platform or be custom-built?

options.name: Native stack options in Expo Router
options.effect: Runs on the platform side, keeps the back gesture, matches other apps.

options.name: Rebuilt in JS
options.when: Never, per the Never Ship table.

decisions.recommendation: Native stack animation, platform default duration; tabs use animation: 'none'.
decisions.evidence: 3. Pick the tool: Screen to screen; Never Ship

decisions.question: Which haptic fits which moment?

options.name: Haptics.selectionAsync()
options.when: A value ticks past a step: picker, slider detent, segmented control.

options.name: impactAsync(Light)
options.when: Snaps home, a sheet detent catches, a drag commits.

options.name: impactAsync(Medium)
options.when: A heavy object lands, a destructive action fires.

decisions.recommendation: Map haptics to these moments, fire in the same frame as the visual, once per user action, never as the only feedback.

options.name: Fewer and gentler
options.effect: Keep opacity and color changes that explain a state change; drop translation, scale, parallax and overshoot; screen transitions fade.

options.name: Zero motion
options.when: The source says reduced motion is not zero.

decisions.question: How should pressables give feedback on Android?

options.name: Android ripple
options.effect: Material press feedback on Android only.

options.name: Same scale on both platforms
options.effect: scale 0.97 on press-in on iOS and Android.

decisions.recommendation: Ripple only in a Material-styled app; otherwise the same scale on both platforms is more coherent.
decisions.evidence: Android ripple only in a Material-styled app.

decisions.question: How should a pill or progress fill change size?

options.name: Animate width
options.effect: Keeps the corner radius intact; allowed because the element is absolute and childless.
options.when: Absolutely positioned element with no children.

options.name: Animate scaleX
options.effect: Smears the corner radius into ovals.
options.when: Not for rounded pills, per the source.

decisions.recommendation: Animate width for an absolutely positioned, childless element; transform and opacity everywhere else.
decisions.evidence: The one exception: an absolutely positioned element with no children

process.detail: Place the interaction in a tier: 100+ times/day gets no animation, tens of times/day gets under 150ms or nothing, occasional gets standard motion, rare gets the delight budget. If it fails, say so and write nothing.
One word: feedback, spatial consistency, state indication, preventing a jarring change, explanation, or delight (rare tier only). If you can't name it, don't build it.
Walk the tool table: CSS transition, CSS animation, layout animation, shared value + gesture, or a native platform component; install with npx expo install.
transform and opacity only, except width on an absolute childless element; never scale(0); translate before scale; no animated elevation or BlurView intensity.
Spring if a finger was involved (duration + dampingRatio from the table, pass velocity); otherwise the custom ease-out, ease-in-out or linear curve with a duration from the table.

process.step: Keep it off the JS thread
process.detail: Shared values and useAnimatedStyle; no setState or scheduleOnRN per frame; no shared-value reads or writes in render; .get()/.set(); 'worklet' in helpers.
Feedback on press-in, commit on press-out, scale 0.97 in 100–150ms, 44×44pt / 48dp target with hitSlop, pressRetentionOffset.
Pick the call from the moment table; fire in the same frame as the visual, once per action, never as the only feedback; schedule back from worklets.
useReducedMotion or ReduceMotion.System; keep opacity and color, drop movement; screen transitions fade; no hardcoded heights.
Expo-installed Reanimated and worklets, GestureHandlerRootView at the root, New Architecture, CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone for 120fps.
Release build on the slowest supported device: flick it, interrupt it mid-flight, reverse it, run it on the slowest Android.
Gate result, ingredients (tool, properties, curve or spring and duration, thread), and what to feel-check; the code is the deliverable.

examples.what: Tab pill and progress bar fill
examples.visual_note: Absolutely positioned, childless elements where animating width is allowed because nothing else re-lays-out and the corner radius stays round, unlike scaleX.

examples.what: Sheet moved by its own height
examples.visual_note: translateY('100%') moves a sheet by its own height whatever its content.
Overshoot feels right on a card that was flicked and wrong on a menu that faded in.
useReducedMotion() sets the starting shared value, or withSpring(0, { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System }) lets each animation decide.
{ expo: { ios: { infoPlist: { CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone: true } } } } lifts the 60fps cap.

caveats: Pinned to commit 85e8e23; the APIs are version-specific (Reanimated 4, react-native-worklets scheduleOnRN, runOnJS deprecated, headerLargeTitle deprecated, NativeTabs under expo-router/unstable-native-tabs) and may change.
'Recent Expo SDKs set it by default' (CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone) depends on the SDK version; the source says to confirm it.
Link.Menu / Link.Preview and headerLargeTitleEnabled are iOS-only.
The 'Initial Response' and 'Output' sections are instructions for an AI agent using the skill, not design rules.
'Never present motion options as a menu' is aimed at implementation; it can pull against OpenDesigner's interview, which offers visual options for system-level decisions [inferred].
The 20fps on a three-year-old Android figure is illustrative, not a cited measurement [inferred].
